Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked â€” quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) â€” tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (â†’) either â€” own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese â†’ reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish â†’ reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim â€” unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only â€” never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

NO prose abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn/auth), NO arrows (X â†’ Y) â€” measured zero token saving under tokenizer, cost decode clarity. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never touch |

## Current state

New actions start as valid agent actions. In `ActionDefinitionFields`, changing `type` to `command` removes agent-only fields and stages `command: ''`. The same select interaction reaches a blur or click commit boundary, so `ActionDraftStore.commitDraft` immediately validates that staged value.

Renderer saving and Electron execution currently share this strict definition validator. Persistence therefore cannot represent an incomplete command action, although execution must still reject one. Here, **incomplete command action** means a command action whose `command` field is a string but is empty after trimming.

`loadTolerantActionDefinitionGraph` supplies `echo Missing action command` only when the field is absent. It does not replace an explicit empty string. An empty command must not gain this executable fallback.

## Implementation details

# App Style Guide â€” Kanban / MDÂ² (React + MUI)

How to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components.

**The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). This guide does **not** define colors â€” it tells you **which theme value to use for which role**, and covers the things the theme can't encode: layout, spacing/margins, borders, elevation, and component conventions.

**The one rule that matters:** never write a raw hex, px radius, or magic color into a component. Read it from the theme (`theme.palette.*`, `theme.shape`, `theme.typography`, `theme.spacing`). If a component has a hardcoded hex in its `sx`/styled, it's wrong â€” that's exactly where the look drifts and where dark mode breaks.

---

## 1. How to consume the theme

- **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` â€” MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`.
- **Spacing:** use the 8px unit via the spacing scale â€” `sx={{ p: 2, gap: 1, mt: 1.5 }}` (`2` = 16px, `1` = 8px). Don't write `padding: '16px'`.
- **Radius:** `borderRadius: 1` (= `theme.shape.borderRadius` = 8) and multiples; for the fixed non-8 radii see Â§4.
- **Typography:** prefer `Typography variant=...` and `theme.typography.*` over ad-hoc `fontSize`.
- **Custom tokens:** roles the default MUI palette doesn't cover (column/track surfaces, the strong/hover border steps, `text-3/4`, section-header color, `primary-bg` tint, status colors) must exist in the theme under a namespace (e.g. `theme.palette.custom.*`) with light + dark values. Consume them the same way â€” `bgcolor: 'custom.column'`. **Never inline their hex.** If a needed token doesn't exist yet, add it to the theme, don't hardcode it in the component.

---

## 2. Role â†’ theme slot

Pick the slot by the element's **role**, not by how it looks in one mode:

| Role | Theme slot |
|---|---|
| App background; tinted footer/action bars | `background.default` |
| Column & sidebar surface | `custom.column` |
| Segmented-control / toolbar track, hover fill | `custom.track` |
| Card, dialog, popup, input surface | `background.paper` |
| Hairlines, resting borders | `divider` |
| Input borders, vertical separators | `custom.borderStrong` |
| Border on hover | `custom.borderHover` |
| Titles, values, headings | `text.primary` |

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

We need to check something: some command agents also might need input from the command line, we also need to support this. do we?

## Current state

An idle command-action popup shows status, history, scheduling, and Run controls, but no input editor. `ActionAgentInteraction` contains the existing prompt editor and hides it unless the root action or active chain phase is an agent.

Command input means text entered for one popup run, not process stdin. Transport already exists: `runPopupAction` reads the shared action prompt draft and sends it as `runInput.extraPrompt`; Electron passes that value only to the root action; `executeCommandAction` substitutes it for `{{card-prompt}}` in the persisted command. Without that placeholder, entered text does not alter the command. Linked `onBefore`, `on`, and `onAfter` actions receive empty input.

## Implementation details

* Generalize prompt-editor ownership so root agent and command actions can render the same service-owned draft and editor surface. Command drafts start ready and empty; they must not call agent prompt preparation.
* Render the prompt editor in an idle command popup. Embed existing schedule and Run controls in its footer, avoiding the current separate command footer and any duplicate controls.
* Keep command input keyed by action id, context, and run id through `actionPromptDraftService`. Popup close/reopen keeps typed text under existing draft-lifetime rules.
* Keep `runPopupAction` as submission path. Clicking Run or pressing `Ctrl+Enter` flushes editor text, sends it as `extraPrompt`, and starts the command once.
* Clear input only after Electron accepts the run and returns its run id. A failure before acceptance keeps input for retry and reports through `dialogService`.
* Keep existing Electron request validation, root-only input propagation, `{{card-prompt}}` substitution, command execution, scheduling, chaining, and cancellation behavior unchanged.
* Add focused popup tests for command editor rendering, typing, `Ctrl+Enter`, Run submission, successful clearing, failed-start retention, popup reopen, and absence of duplicate controls. Keep existing Electron substitution and root-only propagation tests.

## Acceptance criteria

* Opening a command action shows an editable input field and one Run control.
* Text entered in command popup replaces `{{card-prompt}}` in root command when Run is clicked or `Ctrl+Enter` is pressed.
* Empty input replaces `{{card-prompt}}` with an empty string. A command without `{{card-prompt}}` runs unchanged.
* Linked command phases do not receive root popup input.
* Input clears after Electron accepts run, including when command later fails. Input remains when start fails before acceptance.
* Closing and reopening popup before submission preserves typed command input.
* Command actions do not prepare an agent prompt, show agent selectors or attachments, or write popup input to process stdin.
* Existing command scheduling, history, status, cancellation, and agent-child interaction remain unchanged.

+We need to check something: some command agents also might need input from the command line, we also need to support this. do we?
+
+## Current state
+
+An idle command-action popup shows status, history, scheduling, and Run controls, but no input editor. `ActionAgentInteraction` contains the existing prompt editor and hides it unless the root action or active chain phase is an agent.
+
+Command input means text entered for one popup run, not process stdin. Transport already exists: `runPopupAction` reads the shared action prompt draft and sends it as `runInput.extraPrompt`; Electron passes that value only to the root action; `executeCommandAction` substitutes it for `{{card-prompt}}` in the persisted command. Without that placeholder, entered text does not alter the command. Linked `onBefore`, `on`, and `onAfter` actions receive empty input.
+
+## Implementation details
+
+- Generalize prompt-editor ownership so root agent and command actions can render the same service-owned draft and editor surface. Command drafts start ready and empty; they must not call agent prompt preparation.
+- Render the prompt editor in an idle command popup. Embed existing schedule and Run controls in its footer, avoiding the current separate command footer and any duplicate controls.
+- Keep command input keyed by action id, context, and run id through `actionPromptDraftService`. Popup close/reopen keeps typed text under existing draft-lifetime rules.
+- Keep `runPopupAction` as submission path. Clicking Run or pressing `Ctrl+Enter` flushes editor text, sends it as `extraPrompt`, and starts the command once.
+- Clear input only after Electron accepts the run and returns its run id. A failure before acceptance keeps input for retry and reports through `dialogService`.
+- Keep existing Electron request validation, root-only input propagation, `{{card-prompt}}` substitution, command execution, scheduling, chaining, and cancellation behavior unchanged.
+- Add focused popup tests for command editor rendering, typing, `Ctrl+Enter`, Run submission, successful clearing, failed-start retention, popup reopen, and absence of duplicate controls. Keep existing Electron substitution and root-only propagation tests.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- Opening a command action shows an editable input field and one Run control.
+- Text entered in command popup replaces `{{card-prompt}}` in root command when Run is clicked or `Ctrl+Enter` is pressed.
+- Empty input replaces `{{card-prompt}}` with an empty string. A command without `{{card-prompt}}` runs unchanged.
+- Linked command phases do not receive root popup input.
+- Input clears after Electron accepts run, including when command later fails. Input remains when start fails before acceptance.
+- Closing and reopening popup before submission preserves typed command input.
+- Command actions do not prepare an agent prompt, show agent selectors or attachments, or write popup input to process stdin.
+- Existing command scheduling, history, status, cancellation, and agent-child interaction remain unchanged.

entries.content: The runtime confirms this is not a small rendering bug. Command processes only expose streamed stdout/stderr and cancellation; the child process handle stays private inside `runCommand`, and the bridge has no command-stdin operation. Once a command starts, the UI intentionally removes the idle editor and shows only Stop. An arbitrary `Read-Host` therefore waits forever from the app’s perspective.

F_264 implemented the wrong kind of input.

The original requirement concerned a running command requesting stdin. The design redefined that as pre-run template input and explicitly prohibited stdin:

- [F_264_check_input_on_command_agents.md](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/design/feature_descriptions/F_264_check_input_on_command_agents.md:25)
- [F_264_check_input_on_command_agents.md](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/design/feature_descriptions/F_264_check_input_on_command_agents.md:45)

What currently happens:

1. The popup text is passed once as `extraPrompt`.
2. It replaces `{{card-prompt}}` before the command starts.
3. The command starts with piped stdout/stderr.
4. The child’s stdin is never exposed or written to: [action_command_executor.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/action/action_command_executor.js:12).
5. Once running, the input editor is removed: [command_action.tsx](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/actions/run/popup/command_action.tsx:48).
6. Only Stop remains available for an active command.

`Read-Host` is especially problematic because its prompt is written through PowerShell’s host UI, not reliably through ordinary stdout. Electron launches the process without an interactive terminal, so the question may be invisible while PowerShell waits indefinitely on its open stdin pipe.

How to fix it properly:

- Preserve F_264’s editor as “input before starting.”
- Add a separate running-command stdin contract.
- Keep the active command’s child/stdin in `ActionRun`.
- Add a bridge operation such as `sendCommandInput(runId, requestId, content)`.
- Publish a structured `commandInputRequested` event containing the prompt and request ID.
- Set the command run to `waitingForInput`.
- Render a running-command input box and Send button.
- On submission, write `content + '\n'` to the active child’s stdin.
- Handle process exit, cancellation, broken pipes, and repeated questions.

Do not detect input requests by waiting for the command to appear stuck or by parsing arbitrary prompt text. For controlled PowerShell scripts, use an explicit protocol, for example emitting a JSON line before reading:

```powershell
Write-Output '{"type":"input-request","requestId":"confirm","prompt":"Continue?"}'
$answer = [Console]::In.ReadLine()
```

If arbitrary interactive command-line programs must work—including menus, password prompts, cursor control, or normal `Read-Host` behavior—use a pseudo-terminal such as `node-pty` and render a terminal surface. That is a substantially larger feature.

As an immediate workaround, accept the value as a PowerShell parameter and supply it through `{{card-prompt}}` before starting. That matches what F_264 actually supports. The existing F_264 tests passed because they test pre-run placeholder submission, not interaction with a running process.

* Preserve F\_264’s editor as “input before starting.” this is implemented incorrectly: the feature only has a value if we prefill the input box with the command we are about to execute.
* lets simplify: add a switch to the command action editor: when enabled, we show the command window so the user can interact with it.
  * in this case, we simply wait for the command window to close
  * we don't stream the output to our ui

That should be possible right? make a plan for it

Yes, that is a much simpler and cleaner contract: interactive commands run in a visible native console, while normal commands keep using captured output. I’ll trace the command-action schema, editor, persistence/validation, and runner lifecycle so the plan covers the exact files and Windows process behavior.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

entries.content:
Yes. The simpler design is viable, with one important constraint: windowed commands must be manual-only because schedules and card-state triggers have no user available to close or answer the console.

## Implementation plan

1. Correct F_264’s runtime command editor.

   - Prefill the idle command input with `action.command`.
   - Use a plain multiline, monospace command editor rather than the agent Markdown editor.
   - Submit the edited value as `runInput.command`.
   - Treat it as a root-command override; linked actions continue using their persisted commands.
   - Resolve placeholders when Run is pressed.
   - Preserve edits when starting fails; reset to the persisted command after Electron accepts the run.
   - Keep the existing `extraPrompt` contract for other callers, but stop using it as the command popup’s main editor.

2. Add `showCommandWindow` to command definitions.

   - Add the boolean to the shared definition field list, loader, validator, normalized definition, and editable serialization.
   - Permit it only on command actions and default it to `false`.
   - Add a command-only editor switch labelled “Show command window.”
   - Remove the field when changing the action type to Agent.

3. Split command execution into two paths.

   - Keep the existing captured runner unchanged for `showCommandWindow: false`.
   - Add a dedicated Windows visible-console runner for `showCommandWindow: true`.
   - Resolve the effective command first, open a separate `cmd.exe` window in the selected repository/worktree directory, and wait for it to close.
   - Do not attach stdout/stderr listeners and do not publish output updates.
   - Return empty `stdout` and `stderr`, together with the actual exit code.

   Microsoft documents `start /wait` specifically as opening a separate Command Prompt and waiting for it to end. Node also documents that detached Windows children receive their own console window. The first implementation step should verify quoting, standard-handle attachment, exit-code propagation, and cancellation with the packaged Electron runtime before choosing between direct detached `cmd.exe` and a small `start /wait` launcher. [Microsoft `start`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/start), [Node child processes](https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html)

4. Preserve lifecycle and cancellation.

   - The action remains `running` while the command window is open.
   - Closing normally completes or fails according to the command’s exit code.
   - The popup continues showing Stop.
   - Stop, project shutdown, or run cancellation terminates the complete console process tree using the existing `terminateProcessTree` helper.
   - Do not `unref()` the process—the Electron runner must remain waiting for it.

5. Reject unattended execution.

   - Extend the existing recursive “requires interactive manual run” check in `ActionRunnerService`.
   - Reject unattended execution if the root or any linked action has `showCommandWindow`.
   - This covers scheduled actions and card-state-triggered actions before a window is opened.
   - A manual remote-control start would open the window on the desktop host.

6. Define the output trade-off explicitly.

   Windowed commands produce no captured output, so:

   - command history records the command and result, but its output is empty;
   - `onBefore` and `onAfter` still work;
   - output-based `on` rules only see an empty string;
   - commit references printed by the command cannot be extracted.

   Actions needing output matching or captured logs must leave the switch disabled.

7. Add focused coverage.

   - Shared definition tests: accepted on commands, rejected on agents, default false, serialization.
   - Editor tests: switch rendering, persistence, and cleanup when changing type.
   - Popup tests: command is prefilled, edits are submitted as the command override, failed starts retain edits, successful starts reset them.
   - Executor tests with mocked processes: correct runner selection, no output callbacks, exit-code propagation, cancellation.
   - Runner tests: linked windowed actions and unattended rejection.
   - Manual packaged-Windows check using the actual PowerShell `Read-Host` script. This should not become a checked-in automated test because project tests may not launch external shells.

8. Rewrite F_264 to describe these two distinct behaviors and remove the incorrect claim that command input is `{{card-prompt}}` text.

No architecture-decision document needs changing.

`- windowed commands must be manual-only because schedules and card-state triggers have no user available to close or answer the console.` this is not something we should concern ourselves about, it is the user's choice how he wants to set it up. we just leave the window open until the user responds. so don't put in any restraints for this. we need to keep it simple.

* `Use a plain multiline, monospace command editor rather than the agent Markdown editor.` lets watch out here, we still need the markdown editor so we have placeholders and such, but lets set the font to mono space
* `Keep the existing extraPrompt contract for other callers, but stop using it as the command popup’s main editor.` I'm not certain what you are trying to say here. what is the 'extraPrompt' contract? if this is what F\_264 added, then we don't want to keep this cause there are no other callers. so we need to be certain here that there are still other callers left.

Agreed on both corrections: no unattended restriction, and the existing Markdown editor stays—only its command-mode typography changes to monospace. I’ll verify every production `extraPrompt` caller and separate agent usage from the F_264 command usage before revising that part of the plan.

On `extraPrompt`: it was not added by F_264. It predates F_264 and is still used by agent execution—for example, Remarkable image conversion supplies its image list through `extraPrompt`, and the desktop agent executor uses it for non-popup and continuation flows. However, the command-specific use has only one production sender: the F_264 popup. Therefore:

- Keep `extraPrompt` for agents.
- Remove `extraPrompt` from command execution.
- Submit the command editor through a new `runInput.command` field.

## Corrected plan

1. Fix the command popup editor.

   - Continue using the existing Markdown editor so placeholder insertion and `{{` typeahead remain available.
   - Prefill it with `action.command`.
   - Render its content in a monospace font when editing a command.
   - Send the edited text as `runInput.command`.
   - If startup fails, preserve the edited command.
   - After Electron accepts the run, reset the next command draft to `action.command`.
   - Agent prompt behavior remains unchanged.

2. Remove the incorrect F_264 command-input behavior.

   - Stop sending command popup content as `extraPrompt`.
   - Stop passing `extraPrompt` into `executeCommandAction`.
   - Use `runInput.command` for the root command and the persisted `action.command` when no override was submitted.
   - Linked commands continue using their own persisted commands.
   - Keep `extraPrompt` in `ActionRunInput` because verified agent callers still require it.
   - For command resolution, `{{card-prompt}}` no longer receives popup content; other path/context placeholders continue working.

3. Add the command-definition switch.

   - Add `showCommandWindow`, defaulting to `false`.
   - Validate it as a boolean allowed only on command actions.
   - Serialize it only when enabled.
   - Add a “Show command window” switch to the command action editor.
   - Remove it when changing the action type to Agent.

4. Add visible-window execution.

   - Resolve the edited or persisted command and all applicable placeholders.
   - When `showCommandWindow` is false, use the existing captured runner.
   - When true, open a separate Windows command window in the resolved repository/worktree directory.
   - Do not stream or capture stdout/stderr.
   - Keep the action running until the command window closes.
   - Complete or fail using the command process’s exit code.
   - Stop still terminates the complete command process tree.

5. Allow every entry point.

   - Manual runs, schedules, card-state triggers, and linked actions all follow `showCommandWindow`.
   - No unattended-run checks or restrictions are added.
   - If nobody closes an interactive window, the action intentionally remains running.

6. Preserve existing chaining behavior.

   - `onBefore` and `onAfter` continue normally.
   - Output-based `on` conditions receive an empty string because window output is not captured.
   - History records the executed command, status, and empty output.

function makeHeader(overrides: Partial<CardHeader> = {}): CardHeader {
    return {
        affects: [],
        after: null,
        agentLogReferences: [],
        changedFiles: [],
        author: null,
        id: 'F-1',
        internalId: null,
        owner: null,
        policy: {},
        references: [],
        status: null,
        title: 'Untitled',
        ...overrides,
    }
}

function makeCard(path: string, content: string, header: Partial<CardHeader>, isActive: boolean): Card {
    return {
        agentConversationErrors: [], agentConversations: [], content, hasFrontmatter: true,
        header: makeHeader(header), isActive, path,
    }
}

const activeAlpha = makeCard(
    'design/F-1-alpha.md',
    '# Alpha\n\nThe quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.',
    { id: 'F-1', title: 'Alpha feature', status: 'ready' },
    true,
)
const activeBeta = makeCard(
    'design/F-2-beta.md',
    '# Beta\n\nNothing notable here.',
    { id: 'F-2', title: 'Beta feature', owner: 'JB' },
    true,
)
const historyCard = makeCard(
    'design/history/2026-01-change.md',
    '# Change\n\nThis body mentions the fox again.',
    { id: 'H-1', title: 'History change', status: 'archived' },
    false,
)
const architectureCard = makeCard(
    'design/architecture/overview.md',
    '# Overview\n\nArchitecture body with the word fox inside.',
    { id: 'A-1', title: 'Architecture overview' },
    false,
)

const snapshot: ProjectSnapshot = {
    activeCards: [activeAlpha, activeBeta],
    backgroundCards: [historyCard, architectureCard],
    repositoryFiles: [],
    workingFolder: 'design',
}

function action(overrides: Partial<ActionDefinition> = {}): ActionDefinition {
    return {
        agent: null,
        appliesTo: null,
        builtin: false,
        command: null,
        description: 'Create release notes from current changes',
        icon: null,
        id: 'action-release-notes',

        on: [],
        onAfter: [],

        onState: null,

        thinkingLevel: null,
        trackFileChanges: false,
        type: 'agent',
        ...overrides,
        permissionMode: overrides.permissionMode ?? null,
        phrases: overrides.phrases ?? [],
        streaming: overrides.streaming ?? false,
    }
}
